metadata.case_name: WONG YIN WA STONNIE v. LEE TAK WONG

plaintiff.occupation_before: traffic police officer on motorcycle duty

source: the Plaintiff claimed that he suffered left knee sprain injury as a result because his left foot stepped on the ground too hard.

The Plaintiff was taken to the Accident and Emergency Department of Kwong Wah Hospital immediately after the accident. The Plaintiff found his left knee was swollen but the X-ray confirmed no fracture at the left knee.
injuries.icd_description: Strain or sprain of other or unspecified parts of knee

manifestations.description: tension of the muscles of the left knee
reduced and limited mobility of the left leg
greater pain on left knee when walking up or down stairs
discomfort and pain lasted for the first half year after the accident
sleep disturbed throughout the night due to the pain and discomfort; concentration and temper during the day affected
reduced participation in outdoor activities such as swimming, playing football and running; social life hugely affected
requires support on waking in order to keep upright

treatments_received.treatment: Attendance at Accident and Emergency Department of Kwong Wah Hospital; discharged same day; prescribed antiseptic; sick leave granted 1st to 3rd January 2006
source: The Plaintiff was taken to the Accident and Emergency Department of Kwong Wah Hospital immediately after the accident. The Plaintiff found his left knee was swollen but the X-ray confirmed no fracture at the left knee. The Plaintiff was discharged from Kwong Wah on the same day prescribed with antiseptic and granted sick leave from 1st to 3rd January 2006.

treatments_received.treatment: Attendance at Shun Lee Government Clinic GOPC / United Christian Hospital GOPC; prescribed analgesic; sick leave granted 4th to 8th January 2006 and further sick leave 9th to 13th January 2006
source: After the expiry of the sick leave on 4th January 2006, the Plaintiff attended Shun Lee Government Clinic GOPC, United Christian Hospital complaining persistent left knee pain. Tenderness at medial left knee was found on physical examination. The Plaintiff was prescribed with analgesic and granted sick leave from 4th to 8th January 2006.
On 9th January 2006 the Plaintiff attended the said Clinic again and was granted further sick leave from that day to 13th January 2006.

treatments_received.treatment: Attendance at Chinese bonesetter; received Chinese medicine for 12 sessions from 6th February to 28th July 2006
source: Then from 6th February to 28th July 2006, the Plaintiff attended a Chinese bonesetter and received Chinese medicine for 12 sessions.

losses.description: could walk or stand for a long periods; reduced and limited mobility of the left leg; greater pain on left knee when walking up or down stairs

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Before the accident, the Plaintiff would spend time with his friends on outdoor activities such as swimming, playing football and running etc. for at least 6 or 7 times a month. However, after the accident, time spent on such activities has been significantly reduced.
The Plaintiff's social life has been hugely affected.
Occasionally, the Plaintiff's sleep was disturbed throughout the night due to the pain and discomfort. As a result, his concentration and temper during the day has been affected.
